proposer.mechanism: Replace base's per-tick EWM volatility estimator with a fixed-WALL-CLOCK-WINDOW Parkinson high-low range estimator. Keep base's entire decision architecture (vol_ratio = fast_vol/slow_vol, p = max(min_prob, exp(-sensitivity * max(0, vol_ratio - 1))), SHA-256 deterministic draw, reduce-only pass-through, sensitivity=2.0 preserved). Replace the vol sensor as follows: maintain two rolling windows of mid-price observations indexed by self.clock.timestamp_ns(): a fast window of FAST_WINDOW_NS=2_000_000_000 (2 seconds) and a slow window of SLOW_WINDOW_NS=30_000_000_000 (30 seconds, matching the oracle's 30s forecast horizon). For each window, compute the Parkinson estimator over the window: vol = (max_mid - min_mid) / (2 * sqrt(ln(2))). vol_ratio = fast_parkinson / slow_parkinson, clipped to [0, max_vol_ratio]. On every quote tick, push (ts_ns, mid) into both windows and pop expired entries (entries older than now - WINDOW_NS). Cold-start: until the slow window has accumulated full duration (now - first_observed_ts >= SLOW_WINDOW_NS) OR fewer than 20 samples in slow window, return p=1.0.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base uses per-tick EWM with halflives in TICKS (fast=20, slow=120). Because MES quote-tick arrival rate varies by 10-100x across the trading day (open/close vs midday lulls), 20 ticks can span anywhere from 50ms to 5 seconds. This means base's 'fast vol' is measuring something with a wildly varying effective time horizon — the 'vol ratio' signal is contaminated with quote-RATE regime, not just price-CHANGE regime. Additionally, per-tick |delta_mid| EWM is a noisy estimator because mid-prices in MES can flicker by half a tick from one-sided quote updates that don't reflect any real price discovery; the Parkinson high-low range over a fixed window is a known 5x-more-efficient vol estimator (Parkinson 1980) because it uses the extremal points rather than every single sample. The combination — fixed wall-clock window + Parkinson range — yields a consistent-horizon, low-noise vol signal that is structurally a different sensor than base's per-tick EWM, not just a parameter sweep. None of the three failed prior runs (signed-momentum, staleness, reduce-sensitivity) touched the estimator-quality axis — they either added skip layers on the existing noisy signal or weakened the curve on it.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero-slippage and zero-commission fill model (mean_slippage=0.0, total_commissions=0.0 verified from execution_algos/vol-regime-sizer/results/backtest-results.json). All edge from realized P&L. The mechanism reuses the existing on_quote_tick subscription — only state is two collections.deque of (ts_ns, mid) tuples. Worst-case bounding: the decision architecture is IDENTICAL to base; only the input vol_ratio comes from a different sensor. If Parkinson correlates highly with base's tick-EWM, the algorithm degenerates to a noise-reduced base. If Parkinson reveals a structurally different regime signal, improvement comes through better-aligned skips. This is the first run in this experiment that does NOT change the decision curve's polarity or strength — it changes only the INPUT to the curve.
proposer.builds_on: vol-regime-sizer (replaces the per-tick EWM |delta_mid| vol estimator with a fixed-wall-clock-window Parkinson high-low range estimator; all downstream decision logic preserved exactly)
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) Signed-momentum (vrs-pc-r1): falsified -88%. (2) Quote-staleness (vrs-pc-r2): falsified -41%. (3) Reduce sensitivity (vrs-pc-r3): falsified -30%. Confirms base sensitivity is near-optimal on existing signal. (4) Trade-tick intensity: rejected in run-3 round 1 as likely correlated with quote vol. (5) Time-based EWM halflives: simpler fix but doesn't address per-tick noise. (6) Garman-Klass: requires OHLC bars. (7) Increase sensitivity: pushes in MORE-skipping direction; falsified. (8) Composite Parkinson + failed mechanism: confounds experiment.

objections.text: The Parkinson formula assumes log-prices follow geometric Brownian motion over the window. For 2-second windows on MES at 1-tick price granularity (mid moves in 0.125 increments), this assumption is badly violated — mid changes are discrete and frequently zero across many sub-second intervals. In a 2-second window with very few mid-price changes (calm midday lull), max_mid - min_mid will frequently be exactly 0 or 1 tick. The Parkinson estimator was designed for continuous log-returns over hour/day bars — applying it to 2-second windows of discrete tick-grid prices is not a clean efficiency improvement; it can introduce its own discretization noise that doesn't exist in the per-tick EWM.

Run 3's falsification has a different interpretation than the Proposer suggests. Base's NOTES.md per-date breakdown shows base's improvement comes overwhelmingly from REDUCING LOSSES on bad days (20260313-20260317) while only modestly improving good days. Base's lever is 'skip during high-vol-induced bad fills.' Run 3 lost trades that were the BAD trades base correctly skipped, then run 3 lost money on those bad re-included trades — meaning base is correctly tuned at sensitivity~2.0 and reducing sensitivity is the WRONG direction. The genuinely untested direction is whether MORE aggressive skipping in the extreme-vol tail (e.g., lower min_prob from 0.05 to 0.01 or 0.0) would catch even more bad fills. Run 3's negative result is evidence FOR steeper skipping (in the right band), not against it.

An alternative untried axis with strictly stronger first-principles motivation: the BASE'S MIN_PROB FLOOR. base.min_prob=0.05 means the algorithm submits 5% of even the most extreme-vol trades. If those most-extreme-vol trades are disproportionately the worst-fill trades (which is what runs 1+3 jointly suggest), then LOWERING min_prob (e.g., to 0.01 or 0.0) — keeping sensitivity=2.0 — would skip more of them. This is a clean, single-parameter test of WHERE in the vol distribution the worst trades cluster. It is strictly distinct from run 3 (which weakened the WHOLE curve including the extreme tail). Crucially it pushes in the OPPOSITE direction from run 3, which empirically lost P&L — making this a high-prior bet.

The fixed 30s slow window is much SHORTER than base's effective slow window (halflife=120 ticks ~ many seconds to minutes depending on regime). This may narrow the dynamic range of vol_ratio and produce a SMALLER skip lever than base.
Deque pruning must be explicit at order arrival, not just at quote-tick push, otherwise vol_ratio is computed over a stale window.

suggested_alternatives: Lower min_prob from 0.05 to 0.01 (or 0.0): preserve base's mechanism entirely and test whether the extreme-vol tail is even more skip-worthy than base's floor allows. Single-parameter test, cleanly motivated by the per-date loss-reduction pattern in base's NOTES and the joint inference from runs 1 and 3.
Time-based EWM (decay by elapsed nanoseconds) on |delta_mid|: addresses only the tick-vs-time issue without introducing window discretization concerns.
Empirical EDA on a train date: verify Parkinson and tick-EWM disagree in a way that aligns with adverse-fill clustering before committing.
criticizer.reasoning: The estimator-quality axis is defensibly novel, but the specific Parkinson-over-2s formulation has a Parkinson-meets-tick-grid concern. More importantly, an alternative (lower min_prob) is structurally simpler, directly motivated by base's observed loss-reduction pattern, and pushes in the OPPOSITE polarity from runs 1 and 3 which both empirically failed in the direction of MORE skipping (run 1, 2) or LESS skipping (run 3). The untested polarity is MORE-skipping-but-only-in-the-extreme-tail.

proposer.mechanism: Pivot to LOWER-MIN_PROB variant of vol-regime-sizer. Keep the entire base architecture exactly (fast/slow EWM of |delta_mid| with fast_halflife=20, slow_halflife=120 ticks; vol_ratio = fast_vol/slow_vol; SHA-256 deterministic draw; reduce-only pass-through; sensitivity=2.0 unchanged; min_ticks=30 unchanged; max_vol_ratio=5.0 unchanged). The ONLY structural change: min_prob = 0.0 (vs base's 0.05). The skip probability curve becomes p = exp(-2.0 * max(0, vol_ratio - 1)) with no floor (clamped to 0 only if exp underflows). In the moderate-vol band (vol_ratio in [1.0, 2.5]) the algorithm is IDENTICAL to base because exp(-2.0 * max(0, vol_ratio - 1)) > 0.05 only when vol_ratio < ~2.5. The change is concentrated entirely in the extreme-vol tail (vol_ratio > 2.5): vol_ratio=3.0 -> p=0.135 (base also 0.135, both above floor); vol_ratio=4.0 -> p=0.018 (base floors at 0.05); vol_ratio=5.0 -> p=0.0003 (base floors at 0.05); vol_ratio=5.0+ -> p~0 (base floors at 0.05). At sensitivity=2.0, this affects only the most extreme regime tail — by base's NOTES per-date breakdown, this is precisely where the worst-fill trades cluster on adverse days.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base's NOTES.md per-date results show that the +383% over baseline is driven overwhelmingly by LOSS REDUCTION on adverse days (20260313-17 the algorithm loses 22.9-54.4% LESS than baseline); good days show modest improvement (+2.3-6.8%). This pattern strongly implies the bad-fill trades cluster in time, specifically during extreme-vol regimes. The min_prob=0.05 floor means base STILL submits 5% of even the most extreme-vol trades — proportionally to base's ~5,000 to ~10,000 trades in the deep tail (vol_ratio>4), that is ~250-500 worst-regime trades that base CONTINUES to participate in. The hypothesis: removing this floor catches the very worst extreme-tail trades that base lets through, while leaving all moderate-band behavior unchanged. Empirically motivated by the joint inference: (a) run 1 (extra skip layer overlaid on vol) lost -88% because the signed-mid axis was noisy; (b) run 2 (extra skip on staleness axis) lost -41% because dead-market is a different population; (c) run 3 (less skipping on EXISTING axis) lost -30% because base is correctly skipping the bad trades it skips; therefore the untested polarity is MORE-skipping ON THE SAME AXIS BUT ONLY IN THE TAIL — exactly what min_prob=0.0 does.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero-slippage and zero-commission fill model (mean_slippage=0.0, total_commissions=0.0 from base backtest-results.json). All edge from realized P&L. The mechanism is the minimum-complexity single-parameter change. Worst-case bounding: (1) The decision architecture, fast/slow EWM, sensitivity, all unchanged from base. Only the extreme-tail behavior differs. (2) Magnitude of effect is intrinsically BOUNDED because base's existing skipping at sensitivity=2.0 already drops p to ~0.135 by vol_ratio=2.0 and ~0.018 by vol_ratio=4.0; the floor only changes behavior in a small fraction of trades. (3) If extreme-vol trades have neutral or positive expected fill, this run modestly UNDERPERFORMS base by skipping some good trades — but the magnitude is bounded by the small population affected. (4) If extreme-vol trades have negative expected fill (as base's loss-reduction pattern suggests), this run modestly OUTPERFORMS base. (5) This is the only run in this experiment where the worst-case downside is bounded BY DESIGN to a small fraction of trades (the population affected is the deep tail beyond what base already heavily skips).
proposer.builds_on: vol-regime-sizer (single-parameter change: min_prob 0.05 -> 0.0; all other parameters identical to base)
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) Parkinson high-low estimator (round 1): rejected — Parkinson-on-discrete-tick-grid concern is structurally valid; the per-tick EWM may be fine if the issue is min_prob floor rather than estimator noise. (2) Time-based EWM (Criticizer suggestion): a reasonable axis but tests estimator quality, not skip-tail-aggressiveness; defer to a future run if min_prob=0.0 converges on PASS. (3) Empirical EDA before commit: with 12 train dates and ~128k base trades, the tail population (vol_ratio>4) is empirically observable in metrics.json post-hoc; pre-commit EDA is informative but not strictly needed for the parameter-axis test. (4) Lower min_prob to 0.01 instead of 0.0: 0.01 still floors at vol_ratio>~2.3; 0.0 lets the natural exponential decay continue indefinitely. 0.0 is the cleaner test of 'remove the floor entirely' and is what the no-floor curve represents. (5) Lower min_prob AND raise sensitivity: confounds the experiment; isolate the floor axis. (6) Replace exponential with a different decay shape (e.g., power-law): adds parameters without addressing the specific tail-aggressiveness lever. (7) Trade-tick intensity: rejected in run-3 round 1 and in this run-1 alternatives — likely correlated with quote vol, near-duplicate of base.
proposer.revision_notes: Round-1 hypothesis abandoned in full. The Criticizer's MAJOR objections on (a) Parkinson-vs-tick-grid discretization and (b) the joint-inference reading of runs 1+3 (which together point to MORE-skipping-in-tail as the untested polarity) and (c) min_prob=0.0 being structurally simpler were all compelling. Pivoted to the suggested LOWER-MIN_PROB variant. Key advantages over Parkinson: (i) zero new state (no deques, no Parkinson formula); (ii) magnitude of effect is intrinsically bounded by the small fraction of trades in the extreme-vol tail; (iii) directly motivated by base's empirical loss-reduction-on-adverse-days pattern; (iv) reads runs 1+3's joint failure correctly as 'skip more in the tail' rather than 'change the sensor.' The MINOR objections on Parkinson window length and deque pruning are moot under the pivot. The pivot makes the experiment a CALIBRATION TEST of base's tail-skipping floor, which is exactly the under-explored axis after three structurally distinct fails.

objections.text: The hypothesis admits the population affected is small (only the deep tail with vol_ratio>2.5). This means the expected magnitude of effect is intrinsically modest — likely a few percent in either direction. If the goal is a high-yield experiment, this is a bounded-impact test. If the goal is a calibration test of base's tail-skipping floor, this is well-targeted. The Proposer should accept that the most likely outcome is 'small improvement or near-base' rather than 'large improvement.'

min_prob=0.0 (with no floor) interacts with the cold-start path. If _tick_count < min_ticks=30, the function returns p=1.0 directly (no min_prob involvement). If fast_vol/slow_vol are None or slow_vol < 1e-12, also p=1.0. So min_prob=0.0 only affects the main exponential branch. This is correct behavior, but the implementation must preserve all cold-start branches verbatim from base; only the max(min_prob, prob) line changes. The Proposer should commit to keeping every other branch byte-identical to base — no other accidental refactoring.

The SHA-256 deterministic draw means the same client_order_ids that base submits in the deep tail (u < 0.05) will now be skipped by this variant (because p = exp(-2.0 * (vol_ratio-1)) < 0.05 in that region and the draw u is also independent of vol_ratio). The variant's submission set is a STRICT SUBSET of base's. This is the cleanest possible test of the tail-skipping lever — any P&L delta is attributable solely to the trades removed (no new trades added). This strict-subset property bounds upside as well as downside, which is consistent with the bounded-impact framing above.

criticizer.reasoning: The lower-min_prob pivot is structurally clean, isolates a single under-tested parameter axis (min_prob floor), is directly motivated by base's per-date loss-reduction pattern, and reads runs 1+3's joint failure correctly as a 'skip more in the tail' signal. The submission set is a strict subset of base's, so worst-case downside is bounded by the population of deep-tail trades being removed (small). No BLOCKING or MAJOR objections remain. Remaining concerns are MINOR (bounded effect magnitude, cold-start branch preservation, strict-subset property). No clearly superior untried alternative within current run scope — Parkinson and time-EWM are estimator-quality axes that can be tested later if min_prob=0.0 converges.
